issues.legal_issue: A transferee cannot acquire title through a transfer made after the property has vested in the acquiring authority following acquisition and delivery of possession.
material_facts: The land was acquired, possession was delivered to the railway authority, and the acquisition awards had become final.
The claimants’ vendors purported to purchase the land after the original owner had been divested of title.
The claimants later relied on an agreement with those vendors and sought a declaration of title, having given up their challenge to the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The vendors had no title or interest to transfer, so the claimants acquired no interest through them and could not obtain the requested declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 12 and 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the awards became binding and final as to the relevant matters; after acquisition and delivery of possession, the land vested in the acquiring authority free of encumbrances. A later transferee from a person who no longer has title obtains no interest in the land. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.suit_claiming_title_through_later_transf: A claimant brings a suit seeking title to property through a transfer from another person.
predicates.property_acquired_and_possession_taken: The property was acquired for a public purpose and possession was delivered to the acquiring authority.
predicates.transfer_occurred_after_acquisition: The purported transferor transferred the property after the acquisition had divested the transferor of title.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks title through a later transfer and the property had already been acquired and taken into possession, the claimant has no property interest through that transfer.

issues.legal_issue: An injunction cannot protect a claimant with no lawful interest or unlawful possession against the true owner of property.
material_facts: The acquisition and delivery of possession had made the railway authority the lawful owner of the land.
The claimants had no title or other lawful interest because their vendors had none to transfer.

Although a trial court found the claimants in possession, the appellate court found that possession had been delivered to and retained by the railway authority; in any event, the Supreme Court treated any possession by the claimants as unlawful.
The claimants sought an injunction against interference with their possession.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were not entitled to an injunction against the true owner, even assuming they were in possession, because that possession was unlawful and they had no personal interest in the property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 41(j) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, an injunction is a discretionary equitable remedy requiring the plaintiff to have a personal interest in the matter. An injunction is not issued against the true owner to protect a claimant who has no lawful interest or is in unlawful possession. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: property_injunction_suit and defendant_is_true_owner and (claimant_lacks_lawful_interest or claimant_is_unlawful_trespasser)

predicates.property_injunction_suit: A claimant brings a property suit seeking an injunction to protect possession or prevent interference.
predicates.defendant_is_true_owner: The defendant holds the lawful ownership of the property.
predicates.claimant_lacks_lawful_interest: The claimant has no existing lawful right or personal interest in the property.
predicates.claimant_is_unlawful_trespasser: The claimant possesses the property without a lawful right to do so.

issues.definition: In a property injunction suit, a claimant who lacks a lawful interest or is an unlawful trespasser cannot obtain an injunction against the true owner.
